title: What a second, separate rehearsal runtime needs, and the procedure to create one
whatWasDone: Scripts, definitions and committed evidence were read; processes, containers, volumes, images and
disks were listed. Nothing was created, started, stopped or changed: no runtime, container, volume,
database or bucket, and no folder except this evidence folder; no migration, no SQL, no provider
call. No configuration file and nothing under E:/BhuAayam-data/runtime/ was opened. The only request
to the demo was one GET /api/v1/health at the end.
answer: A second runtime fits on this machine and compose.yaml allows it, but it cannot be created today: 24
values are fixed to the demo, 22 of which collide. The list of changes C1 to C9 is the result; C1 to
C6 are needed before the first rehearsal runtime, C7 before the journey may write.
Not today. Nothing on the machine prevents it (compose.yaml takes the project name, the ports, the
bucket and the database from the environment, and resources allow it), but every script that
creates, starts, stops, checks or fills a runtime is fixed to the demo's name, folder and ports. Run
today, each of them acts on ulpin-demo.

change: One validated runtime name becomes the parameter. ulpin-demo keeps today's values exactly;
^ulpin-reh-[0-9]{2}$ gets the folder E:/BhuAayam-data/runtime/<name>, the project and bucket
<name>, and the one rehearsal port set. ULPIN_PROFILE stays demo. Decide whether the
operator subject (:317) names the runtime.
Start, stop, health and doctor take --runtime <name> and default to ulpin-demo; the
launcher, the marker, the process records and the printed lines use the name. Stop for one
runtime never touches another.
The processor image tag is per runtime (or an existing reviewed tag is reused without a
build), and the environment K3b gave the demo's processors is part of the definition, so a
new runtime's processors equal the demo's and no demo tag is ever rebuilt.
A command writes tabular-paths.json and ocr-paths.json for a named runtime after making a
new learning folder and OCR scratch inside its folder; better, create does it, so that
--create no longer stops half-way at "Demo tabular paths missing" after writing the folder
and the configuration file.
changesNeeded.why: S2: no writer exists; create cannot finish in one run

change: The document runtime builder takes the runtime and its serving checkout instead of the two
demo constants, and checks that runtime's own process records.
One fill script for a named runtime: area, Tower 3 import, prepare and commit, record. It
takes the runtime name, refuses the demo by the C7 guard, reads every id from the previous
response (the plan source by sha256 2b9f8803…), and writes create-once receipts under
E:/BhuAayam-data/task-data/<name>/fill/, never into Git. The area step has to be written
down first: only its responses are retained.
The journey takes --runtime, reads its pins from the fill receipts, writes its output under
the runtime's task-data root, and gets a write mode guarded before any request: name matches
^ulpin-reh-[0-9]{2}$; port is that runtime's and not 3194; the target's health targetToken
is not the demo's; the building's snapshot listing is empty.
A Studio dev port variable, so a rehearsal Studio can run beside the demo's; optionally show
which runtime is served, read from health, so nobody mistakes one for the other.
r2-live.ts and r3-live.ts take the address, ids and output root as parameters, if the lead
wants to keep them as rehearsal drivers beside the Studio and the journey.
